Answers below. All line numbers are at commit `2d01420`.

**h01** — S3 presign refresh runner — every 12 hours (plus one immediate pass at startup) — wired in `server/server.go:162-171`
- Component: `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16-45`); the work is `CheckAndPresign` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47`), which re-presigns S3-backed attachment URLs whose presigned link is within 4 days of its 5-day expiry (`runner.go:85-91`) and writes the new `Reference` back via `Store.UpdateAttachment` (`runner.go:116-123`).
- Schedule: `runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`), ticker loop in `Run` (`runner.go:29-41`).
- Wiring: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)` + `RunOnce` at `server/server.go:162-163`, background `Run` goroutine at `server/server.go:166-171`; called from `Server.Start` (`server/server.go:126`).

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120-180`; protection: SSRF-blocking dial + URL validation — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-77`, `internal/webhook/validate.go`
- `Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`) issues the actual `safeClient.Do(req)`. Async callers enqueue via `PostAsync` (`webhook.go:184-196`) onto a 128-slot channel drained by 4 goroutines (`webhook.go:39-55`) that call `Post`.
- Protection: the shared client's transport uses `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37, 59-77`), which resolves the host and rejects any reserved/private IP at dial time (defeating DNS rebinding). Ranges are in `reservedCIDRs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:14-36`, incl. `169.254.0.0/16` IMDS), tested by `isReservedIP` (`validate.go:44-54`). Second layer: `webhook.ValidateURL` at configuration time (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62-83`), called from `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`. Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`validate.go:41`), set from `--allow-private-webhooks` (`cmd/memos/main.go:49,133`).

**h03** — abstraction: `internal/idp`; implementation: `internal/idp/oauth2`
- `internal/idp/idp.go:3-8` defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo` (the shared provider abstraction/result type).
- `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` is the only concrete protocol implementation (`IdentityProvider` with `ExchangeToken` at `oauth2.go:45` and `UserInfo` at `oauth2.go:83`).
- Dispatch: `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:119-134` — only `storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2` is handled.

**h04** — no; `mysql.NewDB` has exactly one call site, in the factory
- `grep` for `mysql.NewDB` across all `.go` files yields a single hit: `store/db/db.go:22`, inside `NewDBDriver`. The only other `mysql.` references are the third-party `go-sql-driver/mysql` package in `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:17,30,73` and the testcontainers `mysql` module in `store/test/containers.go:42,101-105` — neither constructs the project's MySQL driver. `store/db/mysql` is otherwise imported only by `store/db/db.go:8`.

- SQLite: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` called at `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96,102`, defined at `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:380,400` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN (...)` / `WHERE creator_id = ?`).

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in this codebase. `grep -rni redis` over all `.go` files and `go.mod` returns zero hits, and there is no cache-server dependency.
The actual mechanism is an in-process, in-memory TTL cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`cache.Interface` at `:11-32`, `Cache` implementation, `Close` at `:187`). `Store` holds three instances — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — created in `store.New` (`store/store.go:27-29, 45-52`). Config for all three: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`, no eviction hook (`store/store.go:38-43`; same defaults in `cache.DefaultConfig`, `store/cache/cache.go:56-60`). So user entries get a **10-minute TTL**, swept every 5 minutes, plus explicit invalidation on update/delete (`store/user.go:167` sets, `store/user.go:179` `deleteUserCache`). Note `Store.GetUser` only consults the cache for ID lookups, not username lookups (`store/user.go:149-156`).

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware, per-user or otherwise, so there are no request limits to report. `grep -rni "ratelimit|rate_limit|RateLimiter|golang.org/x/time/rate"` over the Go sources and `go.mod` returns zero hits. The only Echo middleware registered is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`), plus static/SPA middleware on the frontend service (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54,59`). Request-path gating is authentication/authorization only — `NewAuthorizer` + `CheckAccess` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:68-93`, ACL in `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`). The closest things to throttling are concurrency semaphores, not rate limits: thumbnail/image semaphores (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:61-62`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107,117`) and the 128-slot webhook dispatch queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong on two counts: there is no nightly database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler is running at all. `internal/scheduler` is a self-contained cron package (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:54` `New`, `:70` `Register`, `:91` `Start`, `ParseCronExpression` at `internal/scheduler/parser.go`), but it is imported only by its own tests — `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13` and `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`; nothing in `cmd/`, `server/`, or `store/` imports it. The `"daily-cleanup"` job at `"0 2 * * *"` you may be thinking of is illustrative documentation only, in `internal/scheduler/README.md` (Quick Start), not registered code. The only real periodic work is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, wired at `server/server.go:162-171`) — see h01.

**r04** — Premise is wrong: neither. There is no message broker in this project — `grep -rni "nats|rabbitmq|amqp"` over the Go sources and `go.mod` returns zero hits, and no queue is declared anywhere.
Actual mechanism: an in-process buffered Go channel. `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`) is drained by 4 goroutines started in the package `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `webhook.Post` (`:120`). Producers use `PostAsync` (`:184-196`), which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the delivery with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`). There is no persistence, no retry, and no cross-process fan-out — the queue dies with the process.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema, server, or dependency. `grep -rni "graphql|gqlgen"` over the Go sources and `go.mod` returns zero hits.
The actual public API surface is Protobuf/gRPC-defined and served three ways:
- Schema of record: `.proto` files in `proto/api/v1/` — `memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `common.proto`; generated Go in `proto/gen/api/v1/`.
- REST/JSON via grpc-gateway, registered in `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65-125`), plus Connect RPC handlers and an SSE endpoint (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:123-125`).
- Non-gRPC HTTP surfaces: file server `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:122-124`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go:67`), MCP (`server/router/mcp/`, registered `server/server.go:92-96`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:64`).
